```yaml
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: ClusterPolicy

  name: image-provenance
```

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Gauges practical multi-language CI in a monorepo by targeting only changed services, highlighting test coverage enforcement and per-service reporting.

### Key Concepts
- Detect changed services with git diff filtered by language folders
- Language-specific test commands and coverage collection
- Aggregate results and fail-fast if any service falls below threshold

### Code Example
```yaml
name: PR Gate: Changed Services Tests
on:
  pull_request:
    branches: [ main, master ]
jobs:
  gate:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v3
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v3
        with:
          node-version: '18'
      - uses: actions/setup-python@v4
        with:
          python-version: '3.11'
      - id: changed
        run: |
          CHANGED=$(git diff --name-only ${{ github.event.before }} ${{ github.sha }} | sed -E 's|/.*$||' | sort -u)
          echo "changed=$CHANGED" > changed.txt
          echo "services=$CHANGED" >> changed.txt
      - name: Run tests for changed services
        if: always()
        run: |
          for s in ${GITHUB_WORKSPACE}/services/*; do
            dir=$(basename "$s")
            if [ -f "services/$dir/package.json" ]; then
              echo "Testing Node service: $dir"
              (cd services/$dir && npm ci && npm test -- --coverage)
            fi
            if [ -f "services/$dir/requirements.txt" ]; then
              echo "Testing Python service: $dir"
              (cd services/$dir && python -m venv .venv && source .venv/bin/activate && pip install -r requirements.txt && pytest --maxfail=1 --disable-warnings --cov=. --cov-report=xml && deactivate)
            fi
          done
      - name: Enforce coverage
        run: |
          echo "Coverage checks would be parsed here; fail if any < 75% per service"
```

### Follow-up
- Extend to handle missing tests per service gracefully
- Add per-service summary artifacts for reviews

## Why This Is Asked

```bash
# check-netpol.sh (simplified)
#!/usr/bin/env bash

DIR=${1:-manifests}
```

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Security hardening of Kubernetes manifests is a practical, repeatable gate in real projects. This tests understanding of policy-as-code, tooling choices (Kyverno vs Gatekeeper), constraint design for host access controls and image source controls, and CI integration in GitHub Actions with ephemeral test clusters.

## Key Concepts
- Policy-as-code with Kyverno or OPA Gatekeeper
- Constraints for host access (hostNetwork, hostPath, hostPort, privileged containers)
- Image source controls (allowed registries) and imagePullPolicy enforcement
- CI integration in GitHub Actions using KinD or similar ephemeral clusters

## Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: ClusterPolicy
metadata:
  name: deny-host-access
spec:
  rules:
  - name: block-host-network
    match:
      resources:
        kinds:
        - Pod
    validate:
      message: "hostNetwork is not allowed"
      pattern:
        spec:
          hostNetwork: "false"
  - name: block-host-path
    match:
      resources:
        kinds:
        - Pod
    validate:
      message: "hostPath volumes are not allowed"
      deny:
        conditions:
        - key: "{{ contains(element.volumes[].hostPath, '') }}"
          operator: "NotEqual"
          value: ""
```

## Minimal Policy (Combined)
```yaml
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: ClusterPolicy
metadata:
  name: security-guardrails
spec:
  rules:
  - name: deny-host-network-port
    match:
      resources:
        kinds:
        - Pod
    validate:
      message: "hostNetwork and hostPort are not permitted"
      pattern:
        spec:
          hostNetwork: "false"
          hostPort: "0"
  - name: deny-host-path
    match:
      resources:
        kinds:
        - Pod
    validate:
      message: "hostPath volumes are not permitted"
      deny:
        conditions:
        - key: "{{ @ }}"
          operator: "AnyNotIn"
          value: [""]
      foreach:
        - list: "spec.volumes[?hostPath]"
          deny: true
  - name: deny-privileged-containers
    match:
      resources:
        kinds:
        - Pod
    validate:
      message: "Privileged containers are not permitted"
      pattern:
        spec:
          containers:
          - securityContext:
              privileged: "false"
  - name: allowed-registries
    match:
      resources:
        kinds:
        - Pod
    validate:
      message: "Images must come from approved registries"
      pattern:
        spec:
          containers:
          - image: "registry.company.com/*"
            imagePullPolicy: "Always"
```

## Failing Manifest (hostPath + hostNetwork)
```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: insecure-pod
spec:
  hostNetwork: true
  containers:
  - name: app
    image: docker.io/myapp:latest
    securityContext:
      privileged: true
    volumeMounts:
    - name: host-volume
      mountPath: /data
  volumes:
  - name: host-volume
    hostPath:
      path: /etc
```

## Passing Manifest
```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: secure-pod
spec:
  containers:
  - name: app
    image: registry.company.com/myapp:v1.0
    imagePullPolicy: Always
```

## Local Validation
```bash
# Install Kyverno locally
brew install kyverno

# Apply policies
kubectl apply -f security-guardrails.yaml

# Validate a manifest
kyverno validate insecure-pod.yaml
```

## CI Validation (GitHub Actions)
```yaml
name: Validate Manifests
on: [pull_request]
jobs:
  validate:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
    - uses: actions/checkout@v4
    - name: Create KinD cluster
      run: kind create cluster
    - name: Install Kyverno
      run: |
        kubectl apply -f https://github.com/kyverno/kyverno/releases/latest/download/install.yaml
        kubectl wait --for=condition=ready pod -l app=kyverno -n kyverno --timeout=120s
    - name: Apply policies
      run: kubectl apply -f security-guardrails.yaml
    - name: Validate manifests
      run: |
        kubectl apply --dry-run=server -f insecure-pod.yaml || echo "Expected failure"
        kubectl apply --dry-run=server -f secure-pod.yaml
```

questions.explanation:
## Why This Question Is Asked

This question evaluates a candidate's practical understanding of security and governance gating for Infrastructure as Code (IaC). It tests knowledge of:

- Terraform IaC fundamentals and best practices
- Static analysis security scanning with tfsec
- Custom linting rules with tflint
- GitHub Actions CI/CD pipeline configuration
- Secrets management best practices in CI environments

## Key Concepts

**tfsec**: A static analysis security scanner for Terraform code that detects hard-coded credentials, insecure configurations, and common infrastructure vulnerabilities before deployment. It scans for secrets embedded in code and flags misconfigurations that could lead to security breaches.

**tflint**: A extensible linter for Terraform that enforces organization-specific policies. It can be configured with custom rules to ensure consistency across infrastructure code, such as requiring standardized tags on all resources for billing, ownership tracking, and environment classification.

## What Success Looks Like

A strong answer demonstrates:
- Understanding of how tfsec catches secrets at scan time
- Knowledge of tflint's rule configuration for tag enforcement
- Familiarity with GitHub Secrets integration in CI/CD
- Ability to write practical, working Terraform configurations
- Awareness of local vs. CI validation workflows

This combination of skills is essential for maintaining secure, compliant infrastructure at scale.

```yaml
# GitHub Actions: scan SBOM, sign, and publish attestation
name: Security Gate
```

## Why This Is Asked
Fintech workloads handling sensitive financial data demand strict data-protection posture. This question validates your understanding of end-to-end security enforcement—from CI gates that catch misconfigurations before deployment to runtime policies that protect running workloads.

## Key Concepts
- CI gate for manifest validation at pull request stage
- Resource requests/limits for resource governance
- readOnlyRootFilesystem for filesystem security
- TLS secret mounting with tls-cert-<app> naming convention
- Runtime policy enforcement via Kyverno or OPA
- Verification strategies for both CI and cluster runtime

## Code Example
```yaml
# Kyverno ClusterPolicy
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: ClusterPolicy
metadata:
  name: require-secure-deploy
spec:
  rules:

    match:
      resources:
        kinds:
        - Deployment
        - Pod
    validate:
      message: "Deployment must set resources.limits, resources.requests, and readOnlyRootFilesystem: true"
      pattern:
        spec:
          template:
            spec:
              securityContext:
                readOnlyRootFilesystem: "true"
              containers:
              - resources:
                  limits:

                    cpu: "?*"

        kinds:
```

## GitHub Actions CI Gate
```yaml
name: Security Gate
on: [pull_request]
jobs:
  security-check:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
    - uses: actions/checkout@v4
    - name: Install kubeval
      run: |4
        curl -L -o kubeval https://github.com/instrumenta/kubeval/releases/latest/download/kubeval-linux-amd64.tar.gz
        tar xf kubeval-linux-amd64.tar.gz
        sudo mv kubeval /usr/local/bin
    - name: Validate manifests
      run: |
        for f in k8s/*.yaml; do
          kubeval --strict --additional-schema-locations=https://kubernetesjsonschema.dev $f || exit 1
        done
    - name: Check resource limits
      run: |
        yq -e '.spec.template.spec.containers[].resources.limits' k8s/*.yaml || exit 1
    - name: Check readOnlyRootFilesystem
      run: |
        yq -e '.spec.template.spec.securityContext.readOnlyRootFilesystem == true' k8s/*.yaml || exit 1
    - name: Check TLS secret mounting
      run: |
        yq -e '.spec.template.spec.volumes[].secret.secretName | test("^tls-cert-")' k8s/*.yaml || exit 1
```

## Verification Steps

### CI Verification
1. Create a PR with the non-compliant manifest—pipeline should fail
2. Update to compliant manifest—pipeline should pass
3. Confirm all three checks (resources, readOnlyRootFilesystem, TLS) are enforced

### Runtime Verification
1. Apply Kyverno policy to test cluster
2. Attempt to deploy non-compliant manifest—deployment should be blocked
3. Verify policy logs show rejection reason
4. Apply compliant manifest—deployment should succeed

## Key Concepts

- **ConstraintTemplate vs. Constraint**: A ConstraintTemplate defines the Rego policy logic and CRD schema; a Constraint is a specific instance that applies the policy to matching resources.
- **Kubernetes resource requests/limits**: Requests define minimum guaranteed resources; limits define the maximum resources a container can consume.
- **Security contexts**: These define pod-level and container-level security settings, including running as non-root and read-only filesystems.
- **Namespace isolation**: Gatekeeper policies can target specific namespaces using the `startswith` function to match patterns like `sandbox-*`.
- **Comprehensive validation**: The policy must validate ALL containers in a Deployment, not just check if ANY container meets requirements.

## Evaluation Criteria

A strong answer demonstrates:
1. Correct Rego logic that validates every container (not just the first match)
2. Proper separation between ConstraintTemplate and Constraint
3. Working test cases that actually exercise each validation rule
4. Understanding of the baseline resource concept (50-200% range)
5. CI/CD integration steps for automated validation

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Assesses practical policy design for multi-tenant clusters and how to validate policy with real manifests.

## Key Concepts
- OPA Gatekeeper, ConstraintTemplate, Constraint
- image provenance, runtime security, NetworkPolicy, namespace scoping
- validation/testing workflows

## Code Example
```javascript
# ConstraintTemplate.sample
apiVersion: templates.gatekeeper.sh/v1beta1
kind: ConstraintTemplate
metadata:
  name: k8ssecurity
spec:
  crd:
    spec:
      names:
        kind: K8sSecurityConstraint
      validation: # omit for brevity
  targets:
  - target: AdmissionReview
    rego: |
      package k8ssecurity
      ...
```
```javascript
# Constraint.sample
apiVersion: constraints.gatekeeper.sh/v1beta1
kind: K8sSecurityConstraint
metadata:
  name: require-secure-images
spec:
  match:
    kinds: [{apiGroups: ["apps"], kinds: ["Deployment"]}]
  parameters: {registry: "registry.example.com/secure/*"}
```
```javascript
# Compliant Pod/Deployment manifest (snippet)
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: compliant-app
spec:
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: app
        image: registry.example.com/secure/app:1.0.0
        imagePullPolicy: Always
        securityContext:
          runAsNonRoot: true
          runAsUser: 1000
          allowPrivilegeEscalation: false
        readinessProbe:
          httpGet: {path: /health, port: 8080}
        livenessProbe:
          httpGet: {path: /health, port: 8080}
        volumeMounts: []
        resources: {requests: {cpu: "100m", memory: "128Mi"}, limits: {cpu: "500m", memory: "256Mi"}}
        readOnlyRootFilesystem: true
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you test this at scale across 100+ namespaces?
- How would you handle legitimate exceptions or registry migrations?
